tasks.task: Build a sales playbook from what the best sellers do

items.when: When a team needs one short playbook: buyer, stages with exit rules, plays and talk tracks
Before writing, to see from closed deals where the team wins, loses and at which stage
When you have the best rep's call transcripts and need the patterns that repeat across them
When the playbook needs a qualification guide, to see which gaps a healthy deal never has
When the playbook is drafted, to have a fresh reader go through it as a new rep on day three
When the playbook tells reps what to say and never what to ask

tasks.task: Coach sales calls from transcripts and score them

items.when: When you have a call transcript recorded with consent and need coaching notes and a score
When coaching should happen every week and managers score calls differently
When one recording must give notes, a follow-up email and coaching points in one run
When you want talk time, interruptions and habits counted from the transcript
When coaching is a list of ten faults instead of one weak part and a drill for it

tasks.task: Build a battlecard against one named rival

items.when: When reps keep meeting one rival and need an honest page on where you win and lose
Before the card, to compare what the rival's public pages claim with your own
When you want a second card with reply scripts and win themes to compare
When you need the one strength of yours that is also the rival's weak point
Before reps use the card, so every claim about the rival has a dated public source

tasks.task: Write a discovery call plan and question bank

items.when: Before a first or second call, to plan listening more, pitching less and a clear next step
When you need a bank of questions for one buyer type, grouped by what each uncovers
When you want a second plan with buyer questions and follow-ups to compare
When the plan should build on the notes from the last call with this buyer
When the questions find the problem but never what it costs the buyer

tasks.task: Write an objection handling guide

items.when: When you have the doubts buyers raise and need an answer with proof for each
When you want the toughest objections found and answered a second way, with gaps admitted
When a rep pastes what a buyer just said and needs what it means and a reply
When the answers are drafted, to find any that lean on pressure or a claim that is not true

tasks.task: Write a win plan and close plan for one live deal

items.when: When one deal matters a lot and you need who decides, what could block it and this week's moves
Before the plan, to map the people, their influence and mood, and who is missing
When the buyer should share a dated plan from today to signature
When a known rival is in the deal and the plan must answer them directly
When the plan is drafted, to score the deal and list the qualification gaps left

tasks.task: Write a rescue plan for a stalled deal

items.when: First, to tell whether the buyer doubts you, is stuck researching or fears a mistake
When you want the likely reason, a firm recommendation and the follow-up to send
When the deal needs safety nets and easy-yes questions, not another chase email

tasks.task: Prepare a negotiation plan and price conversation

items.when: Before a price or contract talk, to set what you want, what you can trade and where you walk
When you need opening lines, questions to ask and what to listen for on the call
When the other side is far bigger and you need the order to move in
When a demand or low offer arrives and you want questions that push back without a flat no
Before the real talk, to rehearse it round by round and see where the plan gives way
When the plan is all your arguments and nothing about how the other side sees it

tasks.task: Build a sales deck from the buyer's problem

items.when: When the deck is a list of features and needs to run from problem to proof to a next step
Before the slides, to outline how belief builds and where the decision is asked for
When the deck has no look, to compare three slide directions made at real size
When the client needs a real PowerPoint file with editable text, tables and charts
When the deck is drafted, to find the flat stretches where the buyer stops listening
Before the meeting, to check slide count, talk time and type size against the slot
When the deck is about the seller and the buyer is never the one who changes

tasks.task: Write a one-page sell sheet for one product or service

items.when: When product data exists and a buyer needs one page they can understand and pass on
When the page is a leave-behind for one account and must use no made-up numbers
Before writing, to fix what the buyer gains, one incentive and proof from a similar customer
When the sheet needs a layout, to compare three directions at real page size
When a line on the sheet could be about any supplier
Before print, to read the sheet as a distributor's buyer with thirty seconds to spare

tasks.task: Write a spec sheet, line card or application note

items.when: When engineers need a sheet they can quote from, with tables and options from your data
When the source is a manual, to pull its own terms and phrases before you write
When the sheet template needs a grid, a short type list and room for dense tables
When an application note should tell how one customer used the product and what resulted
Before release, so every rating, tolerance and standard traces to a test report or data file

tasks.task: Review won and lost deals with the four forces

items.when: When deals are lost to doing nothing and you want pushes, pulls, worries and habits mapped
When you need a script to interview recent buyers from first thought to first use
When interview notes are in and each buying story needs its forces marked
When the worries and habits are known and each needs a fix and one small change to test
When the review lists features buyers liked and misses what they were struggling with

tasks.task: Build a 30-day rep onboarding and certification plan

items.when: When new reps start and need week-by-week sessions and goals a manager can hear on a call
When a hire is confirmed, or a playbook exists that nobody practises
When the plan must start from ranked skill gaps with a learning objective for each
After the 30 days, to compare real calls with what was taught and list the gaps

tasks.task: Write role-plays, recall quizzes and practice drills

items.when: When the drills must match the certification goals in the onboarding plan
When reps should recall product and process facts in short quizzes at three levels
When a rep should explain the product to a curious beginner and find what they cannot explain
When a rep needs to rehearse a hard conversation against an opponent, scored round by round

tasks.task: Write product knowledge cheat sheets and pitches

items.when: When reps need the product's own terms and phrases on one sorted sheet
When the value proposition needs a version reps can say on a call
When reps need 10, 30 and 60 second pitches and an opening question to try

tasks.task: Write a call script or demo script

items.when: When the script is for a first call and should be built around questions, not a monologue
When reps need an opener, fit questions, replies to brush-offs and a voicemail
When the product is shown in person and the buyer should see the result for themselves
When you want a second demo script or one-pager for this buyer to compare
When the script is drafted, to cut lines that pressure the buyer or overclaim

tasks.task: Turn a call into clean notes and a follow-up email

items.when: When a call just ended and you need the follow-up, a team summary and CRM updates to approve
When you start from the recording and want notes, the email and coaching together
When the follow-up pushes for a yes, to try a version where a no still moves things on
Before the rep sends it, to cut the email and check it has one clear next step

tasks.task: Refresh the playbook and battlecards each quarter

items.when: When a quarter ends, win rates against a rival drop or reps stop using the playbook
When each rival's card should be refreshed from the quarter's won and lost deals
When you need last month's real loss reasons and the objection answers to add
When cards and decks quote dated numbers or prices that may have gone stale

tasks.task: Write an honest comparison page against a rival

items.when: When the public page should start from the same honest win and lose points as the card
When buyers search for an alternative to the rival and need a fair page
When the page needs a table that helps people choose, with a fair default pick
When you want to see three different openings for the page as real screens
Before publishing, so each statement about the rival has a dated source

tasks.task: Synthesise buyer or rep interviews into findings

items.when: When several interviews are in and you need the patterns and what each means
When you must show how often each theme came up, with the quotes behind it

tasks.task: Build a business case the buyer can take to finance

items.when: When the buyer needs a low, base and high estimate of the gain with every assumption listed
When the buyer could start small or go all in, to show both with money and dates
Before the workbook goes to the buyer, to catch broken formulas and wrong totals

always.when: Before any sales content ships, so each fact has a dated source, a rewrite or is cut
Before reps or buyers see a document, to catch typos and product names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When a deck, sell sheet or spec sheet must be laid out to a finished design standard
When positioning and messaging are unsettled and the sales content depends on them
When onboarding needs full lessons, e-learning or branching practice written out
When stages, win-loss data or pipeline numbers must come from the CRM first
When spec sheets and application notes need deep technical accuracy across a range
When the negotiation shows the price model or discount rules are the real problem

gaps: No library item builds a sales playbook with stages, plays and talk tracks from a team's best sellers
No library item builds a call scorecard or scores a sales call against agreed criteria
No library item writes sales role-play scenarios with scoring or a branching call practice script
No library item writes a spec sheet, line card or application note from product data
No library item builds a 30-day sales onboarding plan with certification a manager can check on a call
No library item writes a sales deck story from the buyer's problem; only a general pitch outline exists
No library item builds a list of concessions and trades with what each costs and earns
No library item adapts sales training for retail shop-floor staff
No library item checks call recording consent rules by country or state
No library item measures whether reps use the playbook, cards and decks
